questions.question: Labour law exists because:
options: An individual worker negotiates from weakness against an employer who can wait — the law sets floors, rules and collective weight behind the weaker side

questions.question: The Bill of Rights guarantees workers:
options: Fair labour practices, the right to form and join unions, to organise and bargain collectively, and to strike

questions.question: SELF-GOVERNMENT in the LRA means:
options: The parties regulate their own relationship through negotiated agreements — the state sets the framework, not the wage

questions.question: MAJORITARIANISM means:
options: The majority of firms set conditions
The union representing the MAJORITY speaks for the workforce and gains organisational rights — one authoritative voice

questions.question: The LRA is the Act governing:
options: ENGAGEMENT — union rights, collective bargaining, strikes and lock-outs, unfair dismissal, and the dispute machinery (CCMA, Labour Courts)

questions.question: The BCEA sets:
options: The FLOOR beneath every job — maximum hours, overtime rules, minimum leave, notice periods, bans on child and forced labour

questions.question: The floor-not-ceiling principle means:
options: No contract may exceed the BCEA
Parties may agree BETTER than the minimums, never worse

questions.question: COIDA's design trade is:
options: Workers pay for their own injuries
Injured workers must sue and prove fault
Workers get compensation from an employer-funded state fund WITHOUT suing; employers gain protection from individual lawsuits

questions.question: Collective bargaining converts:
options: Many weak individual bargains into one strong collective one — representatives negotiating wages, hours and conditions

questions.question: Bargaining councils are:
options: Standing SECTOR-level bodies of unions and employers' organisations — whose agreements can be extended to the whole sector

questions.question: Workplace forums are for:
options: CONSULTATION inside a single large workplace — elected by all workers, on restructuring and work methods; not wage bargaining

questions.question: The three rooms, three conversations are:
options: Union organises and negotiates; council hosts sector negotiation; forum consults inside one workplace

subtopics.title: When Talks Fail — the CCMA and the Courts

questions.question: In CONCILIATION, the commissioner:
options: Facilitates the parties' OWN settlement — chairing and probing; nothing is imposed

questions.question: MEDIATION differs from conciliation because the intermediary:
options: Actively PROPOSES solutions — which the parties remain free to accept or refuse

questions.question: ARBITRATION ends with:
options: An AWARD — the commissioner hears evidence and decides, binding on the parties

questions.question: A PROTECTED strike requires:
options: Procedures followed — dispute referred, notice given — shielding strikers from dismissal for striking; unprotected strikes carry no shield

questions.question: One worker at the manager's door carries little weight because:
options: The manager weighs one replaceable person against the queue at the gate
Workers may not speak to managers

questions.question: The union's logic is:
options: Many weak voices braided into one strong one — the whole factory's output weighed against the demand

questions.question: The state's role in the contest is:
options: REFEREE — writing the rules and letting the sides settle the score: self-government

questions.question: The three rulebooks answer three days:
options: The ARGUING day (LRA), the ORDINARY day (BCEA), the WORST day (COIDA)
Strike day, court day, appeal day

questions.question: A Saturday job offering conditions below the BCEA floor is:
options: UNLAWFUL in the offer itself — the floor is a minimum, not a menu
A matter for the bargaining council

questions.question: Under COIDA, the injured worker:
options: Must sue the employer and prove fault
Claims from the employer-funded compensation fund — medical costs, disability support, dependants' benefits — without a court battle

questions.question: "Name the day, and you've named the Act" is a technique for:
options: Sorting exam scenarios onto the right statute by asking WHICH bad day the scenario describes

subtopics.title: The Ladder in the Referee's Room

questions.question: The ladder's three rungs, by who decides:
options: Conciliation — the parties; mediation — the parties, with suggestions; arbitration — the COMMISSIONER, binding
All three end in binding awards
All three are decided by courts
The union decides at every rung

questions.question: Most disputes end at conciliation because:
options: The CCMA charges for higher rungs
Most disputes are half misunderstanding — and a settlement the parties built themselves is kept willingly

questions.question: Above the CCMA stand:
options: The LABOUR COURT and the Labour Appeal Court — reviewing awards and ruling on the law

questions.question: The whole machine in one image:
options: Rights on both sides, floors under every job, a rulebook for the contest, a fund for the injured, and a ladder turning deadlock into procedure
